text:
OpenFill

 

 Generative fill, expand and object removal for PhotoCraft and GIMP 3, running on your graphics card. Local generation stays on your computer. 

 
 Remove objects, fill a selection from a prompt, and expand the canvas, right inside your editor. 

 

 [!IMPORTANT]
 Beta. OpenFill for PhotoCraft is at 0.2.7 (that is OpenFill's version; it works with PhotoCraft 0.12 to 0.23) and the GIMP plug-in is at 2.0.0-beta.8, both now with support for AMD graphics cards. Both work end to end on Windows with an 8 GB NVIDIA laptop GPU, which is what I build and test on, and on Linux. A user has also tested all four operations on an RX 7800 XT; see the report. The GIMP plug-in also runs on macOS. PhotoCraft supports Apple Silicon and passed all four tools on an M3. OpenFill for PhotoCraft 0.2.4 fixes Mac typing and model-menu focus, and can reuse ComfyUI's Python; Mac setup and test results. Most of the rough edges are in what the models draw, not in the plug-in; Status lists them.

 Why I made this

I moved to GIMP 3 as my Photoshop replacement after paying Adobe an outrageously expensive cancellation fee. GIMP turned out to be a great alternative, but Adobe's AI image editing tools had become part of my workflow and I wasn't ready to give them up, so I made OpenFill. It now runs in PhotoCraft too. It's meant to feel familiar and easy to use, especially if you're coming from Photoshop. The selection is the mask, the result is a layer you can paint on or delete, and the AI backend (ComfyUI) starts hidden, stays warm while you work, and shuts down when the editor closes. No terminal, no browser tab, no second app to babysit.

Here's what you get:

 
 Fill with a prompt Select, type "a red door with brass handles", Enter. The fill lands on a new layer with a soft mask. 
 Remove background PhotoCraft only: press Cutout. BiRefNet makes the background of the whole image transparent as a new layer. Needs the BiRefNet model (0.4 GB) from the Models tab. 
 Remove object Select, press Remove. No prompt. It erases the selection at your image's own resolution. 
 Generative Expand Drag the canvas edges outward or pick a ratio, and it paints the new border. The prompt is optional. 
 Create A new image or a new layer from a prompt, sized to the selection if there is one. 
 Upscale A copy of the whole image 2x or 4x bigger, as a new image. Real-ESRGAN (64 MB) by default, SeedVR2 for restored detail. 
 

Results always go on new layers, in one undo step, so your existing layers are never painted over. In PhotoCraft it's a panel next to your image (and Filter Plug-ins OpenFill ); in GIMP it's under Filters OpenFill .

 Nothing leaves your computer

Generation runs in ComfyUI on your machine, listening on 127.0.0.1 only. The network comes into it only when you search for models or press Download (a model, or ComfyUI itself). Every file is checked against its size and SHA-256. No accounts, no telemetry, nothing that phones home. Details in docs/security.md.

If you'd rather not run it locally (no suitable graphics card, say), there's an optional cloud setting: OpenRouter, any OpenAI-compatible image service, or Google Gemini (PhotoCraft), with your own API key. It's off unless you pick it, and while it's on, every screen says your image is sent to that service. See docs/cloud.md.

Got a gaming PC and edit on a laptop? Remote GPU runs ComfyUI on the PC and OpenFill on the laptop, over Tailscale or SSH, with a pairing code. Your picture goes only to that PC. See docs/remote-gpu.md.

 Install

You need an NVIDIA graphics card or an AMD Radeon RX 7000 or newer (8 GB for the best models; Remove and SD 1.5 run on less) and Windows 10/11 or Linux. Apple Silicon Macs are also supported; see Mac setup. On Windows, OpenFill can download ComfyUI for you, including ComfyUI's version for AMD cards. AMD support is new, with one RX 7800 XT user report; see AMD graphics cards. Older Radeons and Intel Arc are set up the way ComfyUI documents but untested; see Graphics cards.

The model manager in the steps below is where you get models: in PhotoCraft it's the gear icon in the OpenFill panel, Models section (the Open model manager button on the first run goes there too); in GIMP it's Filters OpenFill Generative Fill... , Models tab.

PhotoCraft and GIMP each have their own download. Both are on the Releases page, where GitHub marks the PhotoCraft one Latest and the GIMP one Pre-release . Use the link for your app below.

 PhotoCraft: OpenFill for PhotoCraft 0.2.7 · works with PhotoCraft 0.12 to 0.23 

1. Install PhotoCraft. You can reuse ComfyUI's Python, or install Python from python.org if you need it.
2. Download openfill-photocraft-0.2.7.zip from the release OpenFill for PhotoCraft 0.2.7. Unzip it and run Install OpenFill for PhotoCraft.cmd (Linux and macOS: sh install.sh ).
3. Open PhotoCraft with OpenFill . The first time, the panel offers Download ComfyUI on Windows (or Choose folder if you have it) and then Open model manager to get LaMa (0.2 GB) and DreamShaper 8 Inpainting (2 GB).

More in photocraft/README.md.

 Patchy (prototype) 

OpenFill also runs as a companion app of Patchy, from its Plugins Companions menu, with the same panel. It needs Patchy 1.25 or newer. See patchy/README.md.

 GIMP 3.2 

1. Download openfill-2.0.0-beta.8.zip from the release OpenFill 2.0.0-beta.8. That release is the GIMP plug-in only; the PhotoCraft download is the one above. Unzip it and run Install OpenFill.cmd (or drag the gimp-openfill folder into GIMP's plug-ins folder; macOS and Linux: sh install.sh ).
2. Restart GIMP and run Filters OpenFill Generative Fill... . If ComfyUI isn't found, Download ComfyUI sets it up (Windows), or I already have ComfyUI lets you pick one.
3. Get LaMa and DreamShaper 8 Inpainting when the model manager opens. The first request starts the backend in about a minute; after that it's seconds.

 
 macOS, Linux, manual install and script options 

See docs/install.md.

 

 Models

OpenFill doesn't ship a mod
